_about: Sites the Red Carpet guide is built from. Each is a grabber in the open iptv-org/epg project. A site that is missing there, or that fails on a given run, is skipped and reported on the status page; it never breaks the others.
_max_channels_note: Raised from 180 (2026-10-31): epgshare01.online and i.mjh.nz are multi-country umbrella sites (process_site() globs every *.channels.xml in a site's folder, so one sites.json line pulls in dozens of country/provider variants at once) with far more candidate channels than a single-broadcaster site. Watch the status page after the first run to confirm this is enough headroom, not too much.

_sites_note: Expanded 2026-10-31 from 13 to 34 sources, researched and verified against iptv-org/epg's actual channel-ID mappings (not just site names -- several candidates were checked and rejected: jiotv.com and xem.kplus.vn both have real sport-named channels but every one currently has an empty xmltv_id upstream, so they'd add scrape cost for zero usable data; guidetnt.com looked like UK TNT Sports by name but is actually unrelated French terrestrial TV). Known real gaps with no available source anywhere in iptv-org/epg: Canada's TSN (only Sportsnet exists), a Philippines sports-specific parser (Cignal/PBA/ABS-CBN Sports), and South Africa's SABC/SuperSport beyond DStv (listed in epgshare01.online's ZA1 tag but unmapped, so not yet usable). Fox Sports Australia (foxsports.com.au) is left in despite returning 0 programmes on the last run -- confirmed a live upstream scrape failure, not a config problem; i.mjh.nz's foxtel/kayo variants now give Australia a second route in regardless.

sites.label: mjh.nz (AU: Foxtel/Kayo/Binge; NZ: Sky/SkySportNow; SG: Singtel -- multi-country umbrella)

Sportsnet Canada (only Canadian source in iptv-org/epg)

Vidio (Indonesia, confirmed mapped -- Premier League + beIN Sports channels)
